aiSummary: Choctawhatchee Bay is fishing well heading into August, with guides reporting a solid speckled trout bite bay-wide and bull redfish making a strong showing — including a 40¼-inch, 26-lb bull logged just this past week. Water is at 85°F and slightly stained, which tends to concentrate fish in shaded, structured, or current-swept water rather than open flats. Plan around an early start: a 50% storm chance with a window before 4 PM, combined with brutal heat-index values near 102°F, makes the morning tide cycle your prime window today.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans the narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel where bait gets pushed through on both tides. Pilings hold speckled trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum year-round, with the lee-side pilings serving as the prime ambush zone on incoming tides. Keep in mind this is the most exposed spot on the dashboard — it's typically the first location to become unfishable when wind picks up or weather moves in.
bridge.todaysCall: High tide crests around 8:15 AM, meaning the incoming push will be building through your early-morning window — position on the lee-side pilings (east/southeast face with WSW wind at 5–15 mph) to intercept trout and reds ambushing bait in the current. The waning gibbous spring tide will strengthen that funnel effect, so expect a more aggressive bite early. Get your time in before 10–11 AM: WSW winds gusting toward 15 mph combined with building storm clouds could make open water here choppy and unsafe well before the afternoon storm window. If the sky darkens and thunder is anywhere in earshot, this is your first spot to leave — it offers zero shelter.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, plus trout and flounder near the mouth. The oyster bars at the creek mouth are the prime structural target, and tree cover keeps interior water a few degrees cooler than the open bay while providing meaningful shelter from wind and weather. The upper creek transitions toward brackish conditions and can hold bass alongside smaller redfish.
alaqua.todaysCall: The tree canopy and protected orientation make Alaqua a smart choice today — WSW winds at 5–15 mph won't be a factor inside, and you can fish comfortably even as open-bay conditions deteriorate. Work the oyster bars at the mouth during the morning incoming tide, which aligns perfectly with the early bite window before the heat peaks. Slightly stained water today favors noisy or chartreuse soft plastics and topwaters near structure rather than sight-fishing on the flats. With bull reds showing bay-wide this week, don't overlook any deeper pockets near the mouth — run a live or cut bait on the bottom as a secondary rod.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees less fishing pressure than neighboring Alaqua and LaGrange, meaning the fish here tend to be less educated and often more willing to bite. Interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water. Pompano occasionally appear at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer, and the bayou is less protected than LaGrange when weather builds.
basin.todaysCall: The morning incoming tide into high tide around 8:15 AM is your best window here — moving water over the grass flats is when reds are most active, and the lower pressure historically on this spot means competition is minimal. That said, today's slightly stained water will make sight-fishing tougher than usual, so lean on popping corks with shrimp or weedless soft plastics worked slowly over the grass rather than purely visual presentations. With less weather protection than LaGrange, keep a close eye on the western sky — WSW winds building toward 15 mph could push chop in, and the 50% storm window before 4 PM means you'll want to be wrapped up and off the water by early afternoon. If conditions turn, Basin Bayou is not where you want to get caught.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is the top trout producer among the locations on this dashboard, with legendary oyster bars at the mouth and interior grass flats that hold redfish year-round. Deep holes inside hold black drum and sheepshead, and the bayou's protected configuration makes it the go-to refuge when weather builds across the open bay. It covers multiple species and multiple habitat types in a compact, fishable area.
lagrange.todaysCall: Today's conditions stack up almost perfectly for LaGrange: the morning high tide around 8:15 AM puts current over those oyster-bar trout during the coolest, most productive hours of the day, and the waning gibbous spring tide adds extra push that concentrates bait and predators on the bars. Guides are reporting good numbers of speckled trout bay-wide right now, and LaGrange's oyster structure is exactly the type of habitat producing fish in these reports — work topwaters or shallow-diving plugs over the bars early, then switch to popping corks as the sun climbs. The slightly stained water is your friend here — it gives trout more confidence in shallow ambush zones and makes them less spooky. If storms develop ahead of schedule, LaGrange is the most protected spot on this side of the bay and a safe place to wait it out or end your day.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and Choctawhatchee Bay, with tidal flow pushing baitfish up the creek on incoming tides and concentrating redfish and trout in the bends and along grass edges. The creek mouth is a reliable flounder zone, and the upper section transitions toward brackish water that can hold bass alongside smaller reds. It's one of the shorter and more protected fisheries on the dashboard, making it a reliable option when weather threatens.
fourmile.todaysCall: With high tide at 8:15 AM, the incoming push will be funneling baitfish up the creek during prime morning hours — position in the bends and along grass edges early for trout and reds before the tide turns. This is one of the safest spots to be if the 50% storm chance materializes: the creek is short, protected, and close to the ramp, giving you quick egress if lightning approaches. WSW winds at 5–15 mph won't be an issue inside the creek, so you can focus on fishing rather than boat handling. Work the creek mouth thoroughly for flounder as you come and go — the outgoing tide starting around 5:10 PM would be prime for flounder, but that falls right in the storm window, so stick to the morning.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is one of the most productive trout flats on Choctawhatchee Bay and a signature spot for Santa Rosa Beach fishing guides. Summer mornings are the peak season, with trout stacked on grass flats in two to four feet of water. Spanish mackerel show at the bayou mouth on moving tides, and while the spot sees regular pressure, it produces consistently. Factor in extra run time compared to the bayous north of the bridge.
hogtown.todaysCall: Hogtown is where the current bay-wide bite report points most directly: guides out of Santa Rosa Beach are reporting good trout numbers right now, and this is their home water — fish it early. Be on the grass in 2–4 feet by first light and work topwaters or soft plastics through the 8:15 AM high tide, when fish should be pushed up and actively feeding. The slightly stained water favors louder, more visible presentations, so don't be afraid of a chartreuse Matrix Shad or a popping cork with live shrimp. The longer run from the bridge means storms are a bigger logistical concern today — with a 50% chance before 4 PM, plan your turnaround time conservatively and don't let a hot bite keep you out past a reasonable departure window.

mallet.aiNote: Mallet Bayou is a small tributary that feeds directly into LaGrange Bayou, the dashboard's top trout producer, just south of Freeport. That direct connection means the oyster-bar redfish and trout patterns that define LaGrange plausibly extend into this smaller, quieter water, though there is considerably less documented fishing history for Mallet Bayou specifically. Its small, interior character makes it a likely calm-water fallback when wind picks up on the open bay.
mallet.todaysCall: Think of Mallet as a quieter extension of a LaGrange morning — if the main bayou is crowded (possible on a Saturday), slip into Mallet and work the same general pattern with less competition. The incoming tide through high tide at 8:15 AM is your best window, as moving water will push bait and predators into the smaller tributary. Slightly stained water and WSW winds won't be a factor inside this protected water, so fish soft plastics and shrimp rigs slowly along any visible oyster or grass structure. Expectations should be calibrated: this is a lower-confidence spot given limited fishing records, but conditions today favor giving it a look as a complement to a LaGrange trip rather than a standalone destination.

mack.aiNote: Mack Bayou sits on the barrier-island (30-A) side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, well west of the 331 Bridge — plan for a significant run time from the main ramps. It shares the same protected-bayou character as Alaqua and LaGrange, with marsh grass, oyster bars, and a few interior holes, and sees less pressure simply because of its distance from most boat ramps. Hewett Bayou and Buck Bayou sit immediately to the east and are realistically fishable in the same trip.
mack.todaysCall: The long run to Mack Bayou is the key variable today — with a 50% storm chance before 4 PM and WSW winds up to 15 mph, crossing the open bay adds real risk if timing goes wrong. If you go, make the run early (pre-sunrise ideally) and commit to being off the open water by midday at the latest. Once there, fish the incoming tide through the 8:15 AM high on the oyster bars and grass-edge structure for trout and reds — the reduced pressure on this water means fish that haven't seen as many presentations. The waning gibbous spring tide gives you meaningful current movement to work with. Pair this with Hewett Bayou next door to maximize the run.

hewett.aiNote: Hewett Bayou sits immediately east of Mack Bayou on the barrier-island (30-A) side of Choctawhatchee Bay, near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park. It shares the same protected habitat as its neighbors — oyster bars and marsh grass at the mouth, deeper interior holes further in — and sees light pressure due to its distance from the main boat ramps. It pairs naturally with Mack and Buck Bayou as part of the same long-run trip.
hewett.todaysCall: Same strategic calculus as Mack Bayou applies: the long open-bay run demands an early departure and a firm turnaround time, especially with storms possible before 4 PM today. Fish the morning high tide on the oyster bars and grass edges for trout and reds, then work any deeper interior holes for black drum or larger reds as the tide begins to drop. Slightly stained water today means fish will be relating tightly to structure rather than roaming, so methodical coverage of the mouth and edge habitat will outperform blind-casting the interior flat. Treat this as stop two on a Mack–Hewett morning, then head back across the bay well before noon.

buck.aiNote: Buck Bayou is the smallest and least-documented of the three neighboring bayous on the barrier-island (30-A) side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park. Its habitat should track that of Mack and Hewett Bayou — marsh grass, some oyster structure, and a modest interior — but there is less basis to speak with confidence about its consistent productivity. It is best treated as a bonus stop on a Mack and Hewett Bayou trip rather than a standalone destination.
buck.todaysCall: Given the long run, the storm risk before 4 PM, and Buck's status as the least-documented of the three neighboring bayous, don't build your day around this spot — but if you're already out west fishing Mack and Hewett, a short look is low-cost. Fish any visible oyster or grass-edge structure near the mouth during the morning tide window, keeping presentations simple: soft plastics or live shrimp under a cork. If the bite is quiet after 20–30 minutes, move on rather than burning time you need to get back across the bay safely. Today's storm window makes flexibility and conservative planning more important than grinding any one spot.
